contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of how to generate own ideas for artistic expressions on the people based on their history and culture, the environment and topical local/national/global issues
indicatorDescription: Explore and study the artworks of some international visual artists and analyse how their artworks reflect the history and culture of some communities in the world
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to: explore and study the artworks of some international visual artists and analyse how their artworks reflect the history and culture of some communities in the world
competencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Communication and Collaboration; Creativity and Innovation; Personal Development and Leadership; Cultural Identity and Global Citizenship; Digital Literacy
resources: NaCCA approved textbook; TLMs; ICT tools; community resources
rpk: Learners sing, dance, draw, mould and role-play from Basic 1-5; they see Ghanaian artworks and performances at festivals, durbars and in the media.
starter: Greet learners with a creative warm-up clap / body percussion.
Show picture charts and real artworks linked to today's lesson; ask 'What can you see? How does it make you feel?'

NEW TODAY (Week 1): Creative Arts – we explore and study the artworks of some international visual artists and analyse how their artworks reflect the history and culture of some communities in the world
Introduce tools/materials and safety rules for handling them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Demonstration – 5 min): Teacher models the skill using picture charts and real artworks – explore and study the artworks of some international visual artists and analyse how their artworks reflect the history and culture of some communities in the world
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice – 5 min): Pupils practise in pairs/small groups; teacher moves round scaffolding technique and safe use of tools.
ACTIVITY 3 (Creative Making – 7 min): Pupils create a small individual piece on the lesson's theme (b6.1.1).
ACTIVITY 4 (Showcase – 3 min): Mini gallery walk / performance; peer appreciation with 'two stars and a wish'; teacher feedback on creativity and craftsmanship.
plenary: Clean-up song – pupils tidy tools and materials together.
Reflection questions: 'What did you enjoy? What was challenging? What will you try differently?'
Homework: finish or practise today's artwork/song/dance at home with family.
Preview next Visual/Performing Arts lesson.
assessment: Class exercises; oral questions; practical performance; SBA
